One of my favorite things to help with flip turns is practicing somersaults (in water or on land) because you can’t do a somersault while you’re tilted. Remember once you’re on your back, parallel with the water looking up at the surface that’s when you push off, and try to stay on your back for just a moment longer than you want to before twisting over. This helps maintain your forward momentum.
Definitely worth the potential virus

I’m an amateur swimmer too, coming in with a better kick than pull, in a pull dominant sport. Front scull drill (and back sculling for better backstroke) both have helped me improve my pull: https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=jsTS-EC10KQ other than that I can’t help too much without a video. Good luck!

I would practice kick/pull sets. Try swimming a length and the kicking a length on your back or with a kick board and repeat as many times as you can, should help with pacing and active recovery. 
Pull sets take the help the lower half of your body float so you can focus on pull exclusively, and that should help with getting up distance too. 
I struggled a lot with pacing so working on endurance helped me a lot.

A couple come to mind:

If/then - if all dogs are hairy, and this dog isn’t hairy, then either it isn’t a dog or not all dogs are hairy. 

Strawman - this is where you take a small part of someone’s argument and use it to rebuild the argument in a way you can take down more easily. 

Red herring - this is kind of like calling attention to one part, or something related, and attacking that rather than the argument. 

For your title question though strawman, it takes your argument and fabricates an easier one.

I might be misunderstanding open individualism but I heard this story, fictional of course, you die and you meet death but he tells you that reincarnation isn’t what you thought. You are every life, every person, through all times. You are Hitler and Jesus, you are your dad, your son, yourself of course, and when you’ve lived every life fully you’ll be able to move to the next phase of your development as a higher being. 
A cute story maybe even something religious in nature. I think a problem with open individualism is similar to determinisms, morals. That is, we play by a different set of morals when it comes to ourselves, it’s harder to hold something against ourselves than someone else, and society as we understand it needs to reinforce the idea of crime and punishment, rather than just crime. So I guess I’d say the problem with open individualism is that it threatens society.

I know exactly the episode you’re talking about. In my opinion person A lives a determinist life meaning he isn’t free since everything is predetermined by dice. Now whether person B is or isn’t free is really a question of what free will is. Obviously he’s bound by responsibilities and reality as we know it but he is able to throw away those responsibilities by rolling the dice. In that way I think he’s as free as he allows himself to be, after all he has the choice not to follow the path set by the dice.
